choices.label: Make a joke of it
choices.text: He doesn't laugh. Then, a street later, he does.

text: {servant} says a name you've never heard him say before: Delilah. "I loved her," he says. "I still don't know if she ever..."

choices.label: Tell him he deserved better
choices.text: He's quiet for a long time. "Maybe," he says.

choices.label: Just listen
choices.text: He talks more than you've ever heard him talk.

text: Children in the street are playing at soldiers with sticks. {servant} watches, then joins in and lets them win.

choices.label: Join in too
choices.text: You lose. Badly. The children are delighted.

choices.label: Watch from a bench
choices.text: He comes back grinning, with a stick-sword he refuses to throw away.

text: {servant} decides you're too thin and takes over your kitchen.

choices.label: Let him
choices.text: You eat better than you have in weeks.

choices.label: Cook together
choices.text: It's chaos. It's wonderful.

text: {servant} sees a mother carrying her baby across the square, and has to sit down.

choices.label: Sit with him
choices.text: He tells you about Andromache, and Astyanax, and the last time he saw them.

choices.label: Give him time alone
choices.text: He finds you later and thanks you.

text: {servant} finds the city library and refuses to leave.

choices.label: Study with her
choices.text: She teaches you more in a day than school did in a year.

choices.label: Leave her there and come back later
choices.text: She has read half a shelf by the time you return.

text: A stray cat follows {servant} home. Then another. By evening there are five.

choices.label: Let them stay
choices.text: She names every one of them after a Roman she disliked.

choices.label: Shoo them out
choices.text: She sighs dramatically, and smuggles one back in anyway.

text: {servant} goes quiet at a playground, watching a boy of about twelve.

choices.label: Ask about her son
choices.text: "Caesarion," she says. "He would have been a better ruler than any of them."

choices.label: Take her hand
choices.text: She lets you, for a while.

text: {servant} wants to visit a church and pray.

choices.label: Pray with him
choices.text: Whatever you believe, the quiet does you both good.

choices.label: Wait outside
choices.text: He comes out lighter, and thanks you for waiting.

text: {servant} finds an old map shop and spends the afternoon tracing the borders of a world that no longer exists.

choices.label: Ask him to show you his city
choices.text: He traces the walls of Constantinople from memory, every gate and tower.

choices.label: Buy him the map
choices.text: He holds it as if it might break.

text: Unprompted, {servant} begins to tell you about the last day of his city.

choices.label: Listen to all of it
choices.text: When he's done, neither of you speaks for a long time.

choices.label: Ask if he would do it again
choices.text: "Every time," he says, without hesitating.
